rationale.conceptual: The method is a custom analytical model from the paper with several interacting components: the many-body force-displacement relation (Eq. 6), the iterative linearization scheme, geometric description of the fcc lattice, mapping of deformation gradient tensors, and stress calculation via the Irwin-Kirkwood relation. Implementing this correctly requires genuine understanding of the physics and careful translation of the algorithm into code.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is minimal: a single Python script (or at most two scripts) with standard libraries (numpy, scipy) can compute all three loading modes and write the required CSV files. There are no external toolchains, multi-stage orchestrations, or complex data acquisition steps.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing the paper's own many-body interaction law (Eq. 6) with a non-trivial iterative linearization algorithm to solve contact forces in an fcc packing under three distinct loading modes. The physics involves Green's functions and a self-consistent iterative solver, which is not a textbook method but also not a wholly novel algorithm. The pipeline is straightforward: a single script can generate all outputs.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The computation involves solving a small linear system (≤12 contacts per particle, tiny unit cell) iteratively, well within typical CPU capabilities. No large datasets or GPU acceleration are required.
